modern: When you have been forced by circumstances to be disturbed in some way, quickly return to yourself, and do not stay out of tune longer than the compulsion lasts; for you will have more mastery over the harmony by continually returning to it.
original: When thou hast been compelled by circumstances to be disturbed in a manner, quickly return to thyself, and do not continue out of tune longer than the compulsion lasts; for thou wilt have more mastery over the harmony by continually recurring to it.

explained.summary: Circumstances will sometimes knock you off balance. That’s unavoidable. The skill is to come back to yourself quickly and not stay out of tune for longer than the disruption lasts. Like a musician who keeps returning to the right note, the more often you come back to your own steadiness, the better you get at holding it.
explained.today: After a tense phone call or a row at home, you’ll be rattled for a bit. The practice is to notice it and return to your normal self as soon as the moment passes, rather than replaying it on the drive home or carrying it into the evening.
